reads.best: It connects feedback to the skill actually loaded and applies approved edits through Hermes tooling with stale-draft checks.
reads.worst: Message-range attribution can mistake unrelated bot messages for replies, and undo overwrites subsequent skill edits while staged writes are not tracked to final approval.

reads.best: Ambitious, product-grade pipeline with a Desktop studio, consented SHA-pinned Blender download, network-off capture and over a thousand tests.
reads.worst: Heavy dependencies (Chromium, ffmpeg) and no cost cap or confirmation before a Directed film the README itself puts at several dollars of model usage.

reads.best: Finished product with seven presets, Desktop studio, and real session diffs as proof.
reads.worst: Heavy dependencies (Chromium, ffmpeg, optional Blender download) and AGPL licence; not run, so reliability is unverified.

reads.best: It is an unusually complete product with Desktop, chat, customer web pages, PDFs, pricing tests, explicit approval before sending, and protections against unpriced extra work.
reads.worst: It has many stateful surfaces, email/web-server/payment-adjacent integrations, and a very broad codebase, so deployment and edge-case reliability remain substantial risks.

reads.best: Decimal pricing, unpriced-item blocking, approval gates and a tested quote lifecycle turn a concrete business workflow into a usable product.
reads.worst: Its audience is specialized, and external customer acceptance requires an owner-provided public URL or tunnel rather than working remotely out of the box.

reads.best: It makes remote release supervision and explicit phone approval a first-class Hermes workflow with durable state and careful disclosure.
reads.worst: Several headline capabilities—deployment, sign-in, deep links, and live progress—are explicitly unverified and require substantial external infrastructure.

reads.best: Uses Hermes’s native approval transport with exact action matching, bounded waits and durable replay prevention instead of treating ordinary phone replies as permission.
reads.worst: The complete live product path remains unfinished in verification: Worker deployment, App sign-in, deep links and live progress are explicitly unverified.

reads.best: It replaces Hermes's memory layer with consolidation that runs in the background, with real guard rails (path limits, size caps, backups, lock file) and an FTS5 store.
reads.worst: Relies heavily on the LLM dream pass, has no UI, and treats tool output as evidence, so fetched web text could be persisted into memory; its tests sit outside the plugin folder.

reads.best: Provider-level capture, automatic recall and bounded file-operation consolidation directly improve continuity across Hermes sessions.
reads.worst: Correction is still model judgment over retrieved excerpts; the reported gains come from small tests on one model and do not establish robust general memory accuracy.

reads.best: It creates a practical regression loop for self-modifying skills while explicitly distinguishing first runs, regressions, judge failures, snapshots, and human promotion.
reads.worst: The child sessions share the real environment and the LLM judge can be unavailable, so its safety and verdict quality depend on Hermes lifecycle behavior and careful review.

reads.best: Directly improves Hermes self-improvement with revision tracking, zero-tool child sessions, timeout cancellation and reversible user-invoked restores.
reads.worst: Its optional judge uses bool(payload["passed"]), so a JSON string "false" becomes a pass; tool-less, truncated skill replays also cannot verify real tool behavior.

reads.best: It turns demonstrations into an enforceable, versioned action gate rather than a prompt promise, with bounded state, approval-aware capture, and extensive semantic tests.
reads.worst: The safety logic is subtle and host-API dependent; the catalog folder has a concise README and limited visible integration coverage compared with the complexity of the gate.

reads.best: Consumable read observations, durable unproven states and carefully tested atomic storage make a concrete fail-closed tool-boundary guard.
reads.worst: It permits only exact demonstrated actions, cannot enforce workflow ordering or stop alternate tool routes, and cannot undo a mutation whose result fails its evidence check.

reads.best: Its source-bound contracts, separate host approvals, immutable exports, and unusually deep tests turn risky data imports into an auditable workflow.
reads.worst: The careful import-and-replay workflow is specialized rather than an everyday need for most Hermes users.

reads.best: Its canary-based tripwire, attack provenance ledger, lockdown, integration test, and human-facing incident reports address prompt injection as a runtime problem.
reads.worst: The environment trap is inactive on remote backends and error handling in the pre-tool hook intentionally fails open.

reads.best: It meaningfully changes where Hermes runs inference, with shared eligibility rules, reversible configuration, drift reporting, privacy controls, and substantial behavioral tests. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humedini/local-fleet/94cd17d2477f9d1a6f39aeee153be1d25c5b57e2/health.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humedini/local-fleet/94cd17d2477f9d1a6f39aeee153be1d25c5b57e2/README.md)
reads.worst: Health probes submit workers to ThreadPoolExecutor without copying context, yet resolve scoped secrets inside those workers, risking failed or incorrectly scoped authentication in multiplexed profiles. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humedini/local-fleet/94cd17d2477f9d1a6f39aeee153be1d25c5b57e2/health.py)

reads.best: A real simulator validated against ngspice with ~137 tests, plus a Desktop pane and many screenshots.
reads.worst: Its pre_llm_call hook injects a self-promoting hint on loose keyword matches, and the use case is niche.

reads.best: Fail-closed approval transport that also detects tampering with approval settings and blocks /yolo.
reads.worst: Telegram-only, no screenshots or UI, and self-protection relies on command pattern matching.

reads.best: Polished, privacy-disclosed local CV with 66 tests, a demo video and a Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Niche health use, and the webcam and model downloads add setup weight.

reads.best: A real memory provider using Hermes's secret store, an outbox, and ~160 tests.
reads.worst: Depends on a crypto storage network and relayer; the ciphertext verify claim is only a heuristic.

reads.best: A durable evidence lifecycle distinguishes contradictions from outages and integrates capture, reinjection, session-scoped verification and explicit recovery.
reads.worst: Automatic capture covers a limited set of regex patterns, while useful blocking depends on the agent explicitly recording decision dependencies; live Hermes turn behavior is not tested end to end.

reads.best: Role tool guards, stale-worker fencing, bounded repairs and completeness-aware ledger tests materially improve multi-agent supervision.
reads.worst: Real-model coverage is narrow: watchdog repairs have not run on real Hermes, and Gmail, Calendar and WhatsApp connectors have only synthetic-data coverage.

reads.best: Distinctive, local agent observability and accessibility, backed by deterministic composition tests and an included audio/visual demo.
reads.worst: A single registered Conductor owns the session timeline, composer and heartbeat, so concurrent sessions can overwrite or mix their state ([session state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JustSteez/hermes-leitmotif/0d43079e3880a79750d87d07ce759769bd182acd/conductor.py)).

reads.best: Durable single-use generation reservations, profile checks, bounded media handling and extensive boundary tests make paid image iteration unusually careful.
reads.worst: Generation requires extra Hermes tool-server setup and disabling tool search for the profile; the exact URL adapter and final UI lack a claimed full live end-to-end pass.

reads.best: Preserves dirty work and the real index, with hook integration, conflict-aware staged application, rollback regressions and a Desktop review pane.
reads.worst: Redirection covers known file arguments and terminal working directories only; absolute shell paths and subprocess side effects escape it, and apply is not crash-atomic.

reads.best: Careful security engineering: SHA256-pinned binary with no runtime network calls, argv-only subprocess execution, secret-field redaction, and explicit seat-isolation checks.
reads.worst: Its own README states catalog admission is pending on an unrelated upstream Hermes bug, and most of the action surface (coordinates, drag, scroll, screenshots) is deliberately refused, narrowing real-world usefulness.

reads.best: Public hooks carry taint into subagents and enforce a configurable policy, with meaningful adversarial and false-positive tests.
reads.worst: Heuristic detectors miss memory/cron persistence and assembled payloads, taint expires in memory, and documented one-shot hook gaps leave some unattended runs unenforced.

reads.best: Approvals bound to a digest of the exact plan, about 311 tests, and recorded before/after evidence on outside apps (Kist, Flaskr).
reads.worst: A dense, repetitive README and 14 tools aimed at a narrow web-reliability audience.

reads.best: It puts Hermes on distinctive personal hardware through a real platform adapter with loopback-only binding, scoped secrets, bounded requests, and extensive integration tests.
reads.worst: It is useful only with a Kindle Scribe and a separately installed companion diary bridge, making onboarding more involved than the plugin alone suggests.

reads.best: Checks use the child’s own tool history, decline unproven working directories and keep host command execution off by default.
reads.worst: It cannot veto completion, file attribution remains heuristic, and proving test success requires opting into unsandboxed host execution of the child’s cited check.

reads.best: It reorganizes the user's existing Hermes work into actionable cards and resumes each card's own session through the Desktop SDK. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrezmo/1guy-plugin/2bb6728048388a419829af5ab8228f3bb977f03f/README.md)
reads.worst: The backend loads vendored modules under generic global names and explicitly fails if another board module is already loaded, making plugin coexistence fragile. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrezmo/1guy-plugin/2bb6728048388a419829af5ab8228f3bb977f03f/og_core/board.py)

reads.best: The bounded operations, hash rechecks, fail-closed proof gate, and human-only apply path make multi-outcome agent editing concrete and inspectable.
reads.worst: Its filesystem isolation is not an OS security boundary, and model-backed planning is unverified unless the operator opts in.

reads.best: Checks source and candidate hashes, serializes mutations, and tests fail-closed recovery while reserving apply and rollback for slash commands.
reads.worst: The README manual install omits proof.py and worktree_review.py used by registered features; planning is sequential and constrained to move/write operations, not parallel agents.

reads.best: Lifecycle middleware makes reversible coding tangible, with multi-file patch remapping, token-protected local review, selective apply and security regression tests.
reads.worst: A copied working directory and command denylist do not confine terminal code: paths outside the project remain executable and arbitrary scripts can reach the network, undermining the README promise that real disk stays untouched.

reads.best: Compact, well-tested (11 parametrized disguise-detection cases plus concurrency and manifest-consistency tests), makes no network calls, and candidly lists what it does NOT catch in a 'Limits' section.
reads.worst: Only catches exfiltration that touches the planted decoy string; a leak that never references it passes through undetected, as the README itself admits.

reads.best: A substantial local engine produces Gerbers, drills, KiCad and STEP files from a shared board model rather than merely generating design prose.
reads.worst: In drc.py, trace bounding boxes omit trace width but the clearance prefilter uses those boxes, so it can skip real copper-clearance violations.

reads.best: Extremely disciplined safety design (deepcopy, no conflicting params on Anthropic, respects Hermes's own fixed-temperature omit list) with 48 tests covering precedence and each request type.
reads.worst: Narrow value since most casual users never touch sampling parameters, and session overrides are lost on restart.

reads.best: The [budget engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusst01/budget-leash/7b4126703e84826e8ff8a8926432057f7790686c/leash.py) combines model-call cutoff decisions with a persistent day ledger whose updates re-read and add deltas under an exclusive file lock.
reads.worst: The [cap check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusst01/budget-leash/7b4126703e84826e8ff8a8926432057f7790686c/leash.py) uses completed usage without reserving in-flight calls, so concurrent calls can overshoot the ceiling and a priced tool is forecast against the session cap but not the daily cap.

reads.best: Its state machine treats uncertain writes as held operations rather than retrying, with extensive concurrency, crash, identity, and recovery tests.
reads.worst: Protection covers only this one tool and a shared coordinator database; ordinary git, other tools, and separate machines bypass it.

reads.best: Real Hermes speech providers, streaming sessions, scoped-key lookup and resumable batch jobs extend voice access beyond a standalone translation skill.
reads.worst: All processing depends on a paid hosted API, tests mock that service, and returned storage URLs are checked only for an initial HTTPS prefix rather than host or redirect confinement.

reads.best: Finished product feel: Desktop card and studio, size presets for Discord/Telegram/X, screenshots and 27 tests.
reads.worst: Value depends on the Desktop UI and Codex sign-in for creation; the GIF niche is modest.

reads.best: Product-grade Desktop UI with demo video, screenshots and broad Python/JS tests.
reads.worst: Screenshots are harness renders, not the packaged app, and it mostly displays rather than acts.

reads.best: Strong security design: OAuth held by Hermes via credentialed_provider_request, default-deny senders, exec approvals from peers refused and decisions routed to the human.
reads.worst: By its own README sign-in fails on current Hermes 0.23.0 until an unmerged core fix lands, and it depends on a third-party hosted broker.

reads.best: Binds cards to exact tool arguments and uses fresh approval keys, with extensive malformed-markup and accessibility tests.
reads.worst: Risk classification and signal placement remain partly model-driven, and the shell parser cannot see destructive actions hidden inside scripts or nested commands.

reads.best: Novel persistent visual memory with local change detection, ~150 tests and before/after screenshots.
reads.worst: Needs a specific Echo Show running a companion app, and reads the Eye token from a file as a fallback instead of only the secret store.

reads.best: Multiple hooks and vision tools make agent decisions and screen verification observable and actionable.
reads.worst: Its main guard depends on a separate local d1 server the plugin does not provide, while much of the default scope gate only warns and the UI text is personalized to one user.

reads.best: Honest design (no summaries), with tests, Desktop and dashboard parts.
reads.worst: News readers are common and need no model or key.

reads.best: Real geometry checks, hash-bound script execution, detail previews and extensive approval/export tests connect Hermes to a practical local fabrication workflow.
reads.worst: It needs a separately bootstrapped CAD runtime and private Hermes approval/cancellation APIs, and approved Python retains full filesystem and network access.

reads.best: Its [merge path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shikhyy/hermes-agent/5b2a4b4a2c43e8a9b1e7bf8d32484a651bffedf0/plugins/chronos/chronos/engine.py) rejects stale or failed branches, checks for changed workspace files, and routes writes through Hermes with rollback on refusal.
reads.worst: The [automatic verifier](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shikhyy/hermes-agent/5b2a4b4a2c43e8a9b1e7bf8d32484a651bffedf0/plugins/chronos/chronos/verifier.py) selects npm test --if-present and treats exit zero as a pass even with zero tests, so a project without a test script can produce a falsely verified winner.

reads.best: Signature verification, delivery deduplication, capacity handling and app-authored replies form a well-developed workflow with extensive tests and a recorded demo.
reads.worst: It directly stores, loads and refreshes Linear OAuth tokens in linear-tokens.json instead of using Hermes’s required OAuth credential route.

reads.best: Tests (outside the plugin's own folder) cover path-traversal rejection, DB tamper detection, and an explicit 'no execution or promotion' guarantee; secrets like .env/auth.json are explicitly blocked from being stored.
reads.worst: Its test suite lives at the parent repo root rather than inside the plugin's own tests/ folder, an organizational inconsistency, and the README itself flags the plugin as experimental/unaudited.

reads.best: Fail-open with bounded per-turn guard, secret read via Hermes secret scope, and 62 tests.
reads.worst: The plugin folder has no README of its own (it is at the repo root), and scoring sends turn text to an external endpoint when enabled.

reads.best: A fresh idea for agents: tells the model when a file it read earlier has changed, through result-transform hooks a skill cannot reach, and fails open.
reads.worst: Only one regression script for the tests, a config file read outside Hermes's settings that can stop registration, and a README full of internal release caveats rather than setup.

reads.best: Commentary anchors must resolve against actual subtitle lines, and release filtering checks spoiler dependencies before showing a note [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jcrabapple/watch-with-me/adb0c77fafd65d6302e51ea5b3b063cf894ec921/watch_with_me/cues.py).
reads.worst: Optional Jev API keys are written to and read from jev-api-key.json instead of remaining exclusively in Hermes secret storage [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jcrabapple/watch-with-me/adb0c77fafd65d6302e51ea5b3b063cf894ec921/watch_with_me/jev.py).

reads.best: Category-only trash selection, protected-path checks, keeper revalidation and reversible moves make cleanup unusually careful.
reads.worst: Windows supports reports only, video similarity is unavailable, and photo quality judgments are simple local heuristics rather than semantic selection.

reads.best: Local indexing and bounded first-turn repo maps provide useful code context without embeddings, network access or extra model calls. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nnazinwaogu/hermes-cartographer/f8b6739af2aaa2f0da2c7c392e9d69e404deedee/README.md)
reads.worst: Rename traverses every indexed Python file and matches identifiers by spelling without binding or scope resolution, so unrelated same-named symbols can be renamed together. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nnazinwaogu/hermes-cartographer/f8b6739af2aaa2f0da2c7c392e9d69e404deedee/carto/rename.py)

reads.best: Rigorous: it catches errors that cancel out in the grand total, rejects symlinks/FIFOs, seals atomically, and has 8 thorough tests plus a demo through the real Hermes loader.
reads.worst: Narrow niche (integer minor units, exact columns, one tool), with no UI.

reads.best: Local-first spooling, pre-persistence data minimization, deterministic identities and transport tests provide useful operational event capture.
reads.worst: A single module-global controller fixes the first context’s profile, spool and transport for subsequent callbacks, which risks misrouting events in a shared multi-profile process.

reads.best: Substantial readable Rust implementation enforces expiring member grants, scoped collaboration and bounded Docker tasks, with protocol and abuse tests.
reads.worst: The Hermes adapter requires a separately installed binary, and its documented installer fetches the latest unsigned release with a checksum fetched alongside it, so the catalog pin does not fix the executable users run.

reads.best: Four surfaces with store, charts and tests, no setup needed.
reads.worst: README banner is copied from another project and the idea is a simple counter.

reads.best: Caps are checked before signing, dry-run is the default and the key goes through Hermes's secret_scope.
reads.worst: Once dry-run is off it pays with no per-payment human approval, which the catalog reviewer rejects, and it falls back to reading the key from the environment.

reads.best: It uses Hermes scoped credentials and validates command responses, request IDs, redirects and response sizes.
reads.worst: The daemon and approval mechanism are external and untested live, while timeout zero permits an indefinite wait and optional ntfy approvals are unauthenticated by its own disclosure.

reads.best: The implementation turns existing household hardware into an agent display and speaker, with local discovery, media serving and simulated-TV tests covering the main workflows.
reads.worst: Pairing keys are read from a plugin-owned JSON file rather than Hermes secrets, and tv_show reads user-specified text/configuration files without a sensitive-file guard before serving them on the LAN ([hermes_tv/state.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helenn-szn/hermes-tv/0423785699fb856bceb2beed1b49e451f3cc97a9/hermes_tv/state.py), [hermes_tv/core.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helenn-szn/hermes-tv/0423785699fb856bceb2beed1b49e451f3cc97a9/hermes_tv/core.py)).

reads.best: Package tests exercise actual Hermes loading, profile-scoped keys, OAuth precedence and cross-origin credential stripping.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains configuration and skills rather than the hosted search implementation, so server behavior and credit-consuming writes cannot be verified from its code.

reads.best: Its locale-independent registry parser preserves unknown fields, distinguishes defaults from observed values, and has unit and live Windows tests.
reads.worst: It solves a narrow Windows-only diagnostic task and does not change Hermes's platform or core capabilities.

reads.best: The pipeline keeps spending and registration settings in user configuration, caps per-call generation, and leaves skill registration off by default [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigBossRabbit/reapx/1d465e712013b59e396ddcf39a5162d34dfb1976/harvest.py).
reads.worst: The review-then-enable path misses existing output: startup skips registered=0 skills, while reimporting seen bookmarks exits before registration [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigBossRabbit/reapx/1d465e712013b59e396ddcf39a5162d34dfb1976/skills_out.py) [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigBossRabbit/reapx/1d465e712013b59e396ddcf39a5162d34dfb1976/harvest.py).

reads.best: Every money-moving tool is routed through a human-approval hook, and the signing key comes from Hermes's profile-scoped secret reader [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yunganas/hermes-swarm-for-hire/a6d31079e5154a06d2cf03aa4ecafa5281be3cae/__init__.py).
reads.worst: Transaction broadcasting has a request timeout but no status reconciliation after an ambiguous network failure, leaving the user uncertain whether a payment committed [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yunganas/hermes-swarm-for-hire/a6d31079e5154a06d2cf03aa4ecafa5281be3cae/near.py).

reads.best: Simple, clean read-only API wrapper using the Hermes .env key.
